source_refs.note: Sub-heading 'Local Area Network (LAN)' of 1.3 as printed (PDF 8, printed 3).

blocks.text: A Local Area Network connects devices within a small area (as shown in Figure 1.3). This area can be a home, school, or office. LAN provides high data transfer speed. It is usually owned and managed by a single organization. Ethernet and Wi-Fi are commonly used in LANs. LAN is cost-effective and easy to maintain.

blocks.alt: A house cut open with a LAN badge: a router with three antennas high on the wall is cabled to a desktop and a laptop on a table, to a tablet on the wall and to a second router on the floor; the floor router is cabled to a printer and reaches the tablet by Wi-Fi. A TV stands on a dresser.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.3: Local Area Network (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.3).
